claimed_purpose.text: Product goal is session continuity — recovering decisions, rationale, working state, blockers, and next steps without asking the user to re-explain the previous session.
Basic Memory stores entity timestamps in a database and exposes them via API/MCP, with a stated philosophy that important metadata should be in the file itself.
Basic Memory acts as a memory provider responsible for memory policy including prefetch, automatic turn capture, session summaries, and commands.
Entities are first-class in Basic Memory, implying the product is designed to track and retrieve named entities across conversations.
Personal knowledge base of Markdown notes that persist across conversations, readable and writable by both user and AI assistants.
Basic Memory consumes project-local Markdown links as graph relations and preserves its wikilink-native canonical note format.
Persistent memory across sessions so a fresh session recovers prior working state without the user repeating themselves
Basic Memory operates in the memory/retrieval space and has been benchmarked for recall performance.
Lets AI pick up context from a prior session by following graph relations

mechanisms.text: Edit operations support granular mutations: append, prepend, replace by section, find-and-replace within section, and insert before/after a section heading — all operating on caller-supplied current content without reading storage.

On indexing becoming available, search by thread_id and synthesize into an existing note if one exists — indicating a conflict/supersession policy of merging into an existing note rather than duplicating.
Persist: notes are written as Markdown files on disk; a local note write returns 202 before the markdown file is flushed, with a drain step at shutdown to ensure accepted writes are never lost.
The live assistant guide describes the retrieve policy as search-before-answer with capture during work, editing rather than duplicating, and graph context on follow-ups.
Delete removes canonical content then removes or reconciles derived entity, graph, materialization, and search state; deleting only a projection is not a valid delete.
The get_user_id callable defaults to returning None for local/CLI usage; cloud deployments override it to read from UserContext, providing per-user isolation.
Semantic search can be absent even when entities exist; the system detects and warns when embeddings are missing and instructs the operator to run reindex.
Entities are persisted as markdown files on the filesystem and simultaneously indexed in a database with a permalink, file path, checksum, and metadata.
Frontmatter is a first-class control surface: the `type` key drives schema resolution, and any custom key is captured as entity_metadata and indexed.
This page explicitly states what is not implemented: quote highlighting, generic OKF conformance, evidence watermarks, and contradiction detection.
A prior fix addressed provider-boundary L2 normalization for models that do not normalize their own output, with a required reindex after the fix
Isolation is per project; test runs must use temporary Basic Memory config/data and dedicated opt-in cloud projects, not existing user projects.
Logging every turn is explicitly distinguished from useful memory; silent capture of private traces into a team project is flagged as a risk.
Hybrid search combines full-text search and vector retrieval, with optional reranking, as the retrieval mechanism for notes across projects.
Per-project client routing determines whether persistence and retrieval go through a local ASGI path or a cloud HTTP path with API key
Distinguishes three layers: lifecycle metadata, raw transcripts, and synthesized durable knowledge — not a single undifferentiated log
Store: curated Markdown files on disk (not a message log); each file is an Entity with Observations (facts) and Relations (wikilinks)
The project is the core isolation boundary; every entity, observation, relation, and search record belongs to exactly one project.
Switching transport modes must not require migrating knowledge — continuity semantics are shared across CLI and MCP access modes.
Two retrieval modes are supported: full-text search (FTS) and semantic/vector search, controlled by retrieval_mode on the query
Deleting an entity removes its search index rows (by permalink+type) and also clears its vector/embedding chunks separately
Claude Code plugin adds session-start briefings and pre-compaction checkpoints as scaffold layer on top of the store
A search index is initialized after migrations, using a backend-specific search repository wired to the project.
Graph traversal as retrieval: build_context navigates memory:// URLs link by link to surface related knowledge
The MCP documentation scopes expected_checksum to reviewed notes; behavior on ordinary notes is unspecified
Import path: ingest prior conversation logs from Claude, ChatGPT, or memory-json format into the store
Notes have a revision checksum that changes when content is modified, used as a precondition for edits
Comments and suggestions write path: leave feedback and propose changes without overwriting a note
Project-local links must be searchable and retrievable after ingesting an external bundle.
Knowledge stored as plain markdown files forming a searchable, connected knowledge graph
Retrieval improvements are in progress that are expected to affect benchmark scores.
Notes addressed directly via memory:// URL paths including project-prefixed routing
A MemoryClient typed client exists for context building within the MCP tools layer
Lifecycle hooks (harness capture) for auto-capture and end-of-session write path
Ingestion of conversations into Basic Memory uses write_note or batch import.
Reranked semantic search and pluggable vector indexes introduced in v0.23
Partner isolation: isolated workspaces per customer with full audit trail
Basic Memory has an indexing step triggered via bm watch or reindex.
Retrieval is performed via MCP tools: search_notes or memory_search.
Write path: delete via delete_note tool (annotated destructive)
Cross-session context retrieval richer than flat file scanning.
Metadata filtering on YAML frontmatter fields for retrieval

ledger.claim: Store is curated Markdown files (Entities + Observations + Relations), not a raw message log
ledger.quote: Each file is an `Entity`. Entities have `Observations` (facts about them) and `Relations` (links to other entities). That's the whole grammar.

ledger.claim: Write path: markdown file write → content materialization → vector sync + relation resolution, all queued as background tasks; drain on shutdown ensures no accepted write is lost.
ledger.quote: A local note write returns 202 before its markdown file is written; shutdown can land while that materialization (and the vector sync / relation resolution it schedules) is still queued in the in-process pool. Drain both queues before the engine closes so an accepted write is never lost
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Semantic search is optional; the system detects missing embeddings at startup and warns the operator to run reindex.

ledger.claim: Redis read cache is invalidated at startup to prevent stale reads from offline file edits; failure disables the cache for the lifespan.
ledger.quote: reusing any prior generation could hide an offline file edit until TTL expiry. Outcome: disable caching for this lifespan and serve only authoritative reads.
ledger.label: measured
